result.title: The Critic Can Hurt: On the Safety of Critics in LLM-Guided AutoML Search
result.summary: LLM critics increasingly steer iterative search in agentic AutoML, prompt optimization, and self-refinement--evaluated for whether they help, but rarely for whether they can hurt. We isolate the critic's marginal effect through a four-arm audit and characterize the loop's tolerance through controlled fault injection. We show a naive 8B critic drives search below the no-critic random-search floor on 7 of 8 tabular datasets, losing up to 0.245 AUC in the worst case; the magnitude varies strongly with dataset, frontier, and budget. When: stronger critics attenuate the loss on the evaluated suite, without establishing a universal capability threshold. Why: controlled fault injection shows that non-directional errors are nearly costless under best-so-far search, whereas directional errors consume finite search opportunities; an idealized effective-sample calculation yields a necessary condition, $q(m-1) > β$, not a deployment certificate. How: a simple observable validation gate and a learned detector can reduce realized loss, but neither is guaranteed to preserve the full-budget no-critic baseline. We will release CRITFAULT, to our knowledge the first benchmark for detecting harmful critic feedback in AutoML. A critic is not a free addition: audit before trusting, and gate when capability or verification is insufficient.

AI.brief_summary: 论文通过四臂审计与受控故障注入，隔离 LLM critic 对 AutoML 迭代搜索的边际影响，发现较弱的 critic 会让搜索低于无 critic 的随机搜索基线，并分析方向性错误与有限搜索预算的关系，最后尝试用可观测验证门控与学习式检测器降低损失。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「反馈信号究竟帮忙还是致害」的消融审计、故障注入与门控检测，可供核查 VLM 推理循环中视觉或 latent 反馈通道的实际贡献及何时应屏蔽，属方法线索而非视觉推理研究本身。
